market_holds: Spot 10.64 (sealed baseline 2026-11-24 18:08 UTC), 2.4% above the 52-week low and 46.9% below the high; -8.0% over 5 sessions and -5.5% over 20. The Yahoo closes show most of the 5-day drop came in one sector-wide session, 11-20 (LI -7.6%, XPEV -13.9%, NIO -8.0%, KWEB -2.8%), and LI did not bounce afterwards the way XPEV did (+12%). Front-expiry options (11-27) imply an event move of about 5.95%, but the ATM spread is 67% of mid, so that figure is indicative only. Skew is 12.6 vol points toward puts (downside paid) and put/call OI is 0.97. Q3 is mostly pre-released: deliveries were 99,964 (CnEVPost, 2026-11-10) at the top of the 95-100k guide. Earnings Whispers' consensus (2026-11-18) is revenue of about $4.09bn, at the top of the RMB26.6-28.0bn guide, and EPS of -$0.08. The cited consensus net loss is RMB942m. Deutsche Bank is above it: GM 16.7% and a net loss of about RMB300m (2026-11-10). It also published Nov deliveries of more than 40k, including 16-20k i6, and more than 50k i6 orders, so the i6 ramp is a public datapoint. October deliveries were 29,025, the lowest since February. October production was 37,908, so about 9k units were built ahead of November delivery. The ~490k full-year target (Q2 call, 2026-08-26) would need roughly 167k in Nov+Dec against a 30-40k monthly run rate, so it is visibly dead. Recent prints moved the stock little by the close but opened it lower, on guides that came in under consensus. The May 28 2026 print gapped -4.7% and closed -1.5% (Q2 guide below). The Aug 26 2026 print gapped -1.1% and closed -1.1% (Q3 revenue guide about 15% below the RMB32.3bn consensus). The Nov 26 2025 print gapped -2.0% and closed +0.6% (Q4 guide 100-110k vs 135.6k est).
view: The line this print trades on is the Q4 guide, deliveries and revenue, plus the margin commentary, not the Q3 headline, which is largely pre-released. Q3 has a mild positive tilt. Deliveries landed at the top of guidance. The mix moved up with the i9 (RMB369.8k, more than 10k delivered since 09-16) and the new Mega. The CFO guided H2 margin expansion from a 9.4% vehicle margin in Q2. DB's 16.7% GM / RMB300m loss sits well above the RMB942m consensus loss, so a margin beat is plausible. On Q4, the arithmetic is Oct 29,025 plus DB's Nov >40k plus Dec of 45-50k, which gives about 115-120k: positive year on year against Q4 2025's 109,194 and the first growth quarter in a while. The company also built about 9k more units than it delivered in October. Against that, management has guided below the Street on at least three consecutive prints. The 490k target will be formally abandoned. The i6 launch price (RMB239.8k until Nov 30), the doubled RMB10k insurance subsidy on mature models and the memory-chip and battery cost inflation management said it would absorb all point to a softer Q4 margin. XPEV's strong Q4 guide (11-16) bought only a one-day bounce before the sector broke on 11-20. Positioning cuts both ways: the stock sits at 52-week lows after an 8% slide, which cushions a bad guide, but sentiment and sector momentum are poor. I could not see the one datapoint that would decide this, the November weekly registrations for the i6 ramp, and I cannot show that sell-side Q4 numbers sit above or below a ~115-120k guide. I have no edge on direction. I expect a move a bit smaller than the options imply, since recent close-to-13:00 reactions have been 1-3%, with tails if the Q4 guide surprises either way.

recommendation.reason: The decisive line is the Q4 delivery and revenue guide against a sell-side Q4 number I could not find. The i6 ramp evidence (DB Nov >40k, >50k orders, October production 9k above deliveries) is public and dated 11-10, so it is plausibly in estimates. The record of three consecutive below-Street guides is offset by a stock already at 52-week lows after an 8% sector-driven slide. With no unpriced mechanism I can show, I don't think a directional bet is justified.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q4 delivery guide topping 125k with a stated Q4 vehicle margin in the mid-teens would point up. A guide at or below ~110k (flat on Q4 2025), or margin guided down on i6 promotions and chip costs, would point down.

self_critique: Case for down: management has under-guided the Street on every recent print, the stock opened lower each time, and this guide formally kills the 490k target. Q4 margin faces i6 launch pricing, doubled subsidies and chip costs, and sector momentum is broken. Case for up: the stock is at 52-week lows with puts rich after an 8% slide, Q3 margin likely beats, and the first YoY delivery growth guide in quarters could squeeze shorts. Both are real, and I could not see the sell-side Q4 bar, so 50 stands.
approach_notes: Writing down what the price holds and checking the reaction history from bars was the useful part: it moved abs_move below the implied move and showed the repeated guide-miss gaps. The physical-world route (weekly registrations) would have decided this print, but none of the sources I tried had 2026 data.
